title: Process Rewards for Outcome-Guided Reasoning Steps in LLM Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2604.02341v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Mathematical reasoning in large language models has improved substantially with reinforcement learning using verifiable rewards, where final answers can be checked automatically and converted into reliable training signals. Most such pipelines optimize outcome correctness only, which yields sparse feedback for long, multi-step solutions and offers limited guidance on intermediate reasoning errors. Recent work therefore introduces process reward models (PRMs) to score intermediate steps and provide denser supervision. In practice, PRM scores are often imperfectly aligned with final correctness and can reward locally fluent reasoning that still ends in an incorrect answer. When optimized as absolute rewards, such signals can amplify fluent failure modes and induce reward hacking. translated_title: 大语言模型强化学习中结果导向推理步骤的过程奖励
translated_abstract: 随着使用可验证奖励的强化学习的发展，大语言模型的数学推理能力得到了显著提升——最终答案可以被自动检查并转化为可靠的训练信号。然而，大多数此类流程仅优化结果的正确性，这对长篇多步骤解答而言反馈过于稀疏，且对中间推理错误的指导有限。因此，近期工作引入了过程奖励模型（PRM）来为中间步骤打分，从而提供更密集的监督。但在实践中，PRM 的评分与最终答案的正确性往往并不完全一致，可能奖励那些局部流畅却最终得出错误答案的推理过程。当这些信号被当作绝对奖励进行优化时，可能会放大“流畅却失败”的模式并诱发奖励作弊。我们提出了 PROGRS，一个在保持结果正确性主导地位的同时有效利用 PRM 的框架。PROGRS 将过程奖励视为相对偏好（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出 PROGRS 框架，在强化学习中保持结果正确性为主导，将过程奖励模型（PRM）的评分作为相对偏好而非绝对奖励加以利用，从而在不引发奖励作弊的前提下为多步数学推理提供更密集的监督信号。
en_tdlr: PROGRS leverages process reward models (PRMs) as relative preferences while keeping outcome correctness dominant, providing denser supervision for multi-step mathematical reasoning in LLM reinforcement learning without inducing reward hacking.
